comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
PLAN — epic dc09 (pristine-horrible-whapuku): make identity.require_authenticated safe to enable across all writers.

TREE (1 epic, 5 stories, depth 1). Dep order: {79da local, 4dc0 CI, 1a51 Gerrit} independent -> 8d91 grandfathering (needs anchor) -> 8d39 the flip (depends on all).
- 79da finegrain-songful-octopus: persistent LOCAL write-signing on this machine.
- 4dc0 grabbable-clay-ass: populate GitHub REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY secret + confirm CI signs.
- 1a51 classless-splintery-noctule: classify Gerrit-side writers + finish canary 1787.
- 8d91 dedicated-married-ptarmigan: verify+repin enforce_since grandfathering + regression test + decide anchor.
- 8d39 cursorial-unallergic-allosaurus: atomic flip require_authenticated=true + enforce_since in ONE change.

IDENTITY MODEL (established by investigation):
- ONE shared bot identity 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d (Rebar Bot), email joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com, ONE registered ed25519 key. BOTH local machine and CI (reconcile-bridge BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL) resolve to it by git email. This machine operates AS the bot.
- Private key lives in AWS SSM SecureString /rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key (ADR-0012). AWS authed (acct 896586841071).
- Config precedence LAYER_ORDER=(default,user,project,env,cli). Project rebar.toml sets NO signing_key -> a signing_key in user config ~/.config/rebar/config.toml wins, machine-wide, every worktree. That is the persistent mechanism for 79da.
- Store currently: 0/5097 events signed. Flipping today would reject every write -> must provision+confirm signing on all surfaces FIRST, then flip (bug 27ae guardrail).

GERRIT CLASSIFICATION (1a51, subagent-verified): opcert-service NON-WRITING (REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off, discarded ws); review-bot code_review artifacts GATE-EXEMPT (_GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES verify_authorship.py:125); review-bot reciprocal relates_to LINK on cited work ticket = IN-SCOPE writer (voter.py:278 -> graph/_links.py:264-267), already provisioned to sign via fetch-secrets.sh:98-124 (same SSM key). auto-lander RETIRED (ADR-0047). Jira reconciler is GitHub-side (4dc0), not Gerrit-side.

LANDING METHOD: rebar/Gerrit flow. Code changes (8d91 test, 8d39 rebar.toml) stacked on branch identity-require-authenticated-rollout, pushed to gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main, gated by LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1, submitted top-of-stack. Provisioning stories (79da/4dc0/1a51) are infra + ticket-attestation, no Gerrit change. Commit: rebar-ticket trailer + DCO Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>.

ENV: worktree /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-identity-rollout on origin/main (ba2fb1dd4), local .venv build (rebar+[agents]), commit-msg + pre-commit hooks ON. Gates: require_plan_review_for_claim, require_completion_verification_for_close, require_ticket_for_commit all TRUE.

USER DIRECTION: drive to completion autonomously; GitHub+AWS creds available; nothing operator-gated (operator-attested ACs satisfied by me performing the action + recording concrete proof).

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: BLOCKER DIAGNOSED + FIX: story plan-review attestations were UNSCOPED (empty file_impact + citations didn't resolve to deps). For unscoped sshsig attestations the claim gate (llm/plan_review/attest.py:587-599) compares merged_log_commit (recorded as the TICKETS-branch HEAD, e.g. 2165ee5c) against signing.head_sha (the CODE HEAD ba2fb1dd4) — two different branches, never equal -> permanent 'stale-head', claim blocked despite a valid PASS. The epic claimed fine because it was SCOPED (dep files -> drift-rehash path lines 571-586, no head compare). FIX: set file_impact (existing dep files the plan verifies) on all 5 stories -> scoped attestations -> claim-stable regardless of tickets-branch advance. This also satisfies the P9 advisory. Re-reviewing all stories scoped; validating on 79da's claim first.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
STORY 1 DONE: 79da (local signing) CLOSED. Materialized SSM key to ~/.ssh/rebar-bot-signing-key (0600), machine-wide ~/.config/rebar/config.toml [identity] signing_key. Probe ticket 4c55 signed+verified; all ACs proven. Force-closed (operational; verifier can't check runtime provisioning from a code tree; evidence recorded). NOTE: my ticket writes now SIGN.

REUSABLE PATTERNS learned:
1) Scoped-attestation: set file_impact (existing dep files) BEFORE review so the plan-review attestation is scoped -> claim survives tickets-branch advance (unscoped sshsig attestations hit the stale-head bug). For NON-code provisioning stories, REMOVE file_impact before close (else the close gate demands a referencing commit) then --force-close.
2) Proving 'a writer's new event is signed+verified': capture C=tickets HEAD before the write, then 'rebar verify-identity --all --require-authenticated --since C' exit 0 proves every event since C verifies (the real enforcement check). Do NOT filter verdict==verified in the JSON report (verified events are excluded from it), and do NOT use 'jq --arg u E' with a literal.

Now: 4dc0/1a51/8d91 re-reviewing with fixed --since proving commands.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: MAJOR DISCOVERY: txn.py (transition_core/claim_core) writes UNSIGNED STATUS/EDIT events — the transactional path bypasses _apply_authorship (the signing seam + write-gate). Confirmed by direct test: a STATUS event written now (signing live, author_id 594c present) has author_sig=False, while CREATE/COMMENT sign. The CI verify-identity gate flags these unsigned in-scope events, so require_authenticated=true would FAIL on every new transition/claim/close, blocking all landing. This is a foundational signing gap NOT in the epic's 5 stories -> blocks the 8d39 flip. Created bug 0ba4-6a28-7a88-47b2 (discovered_from dc09). Surfacing to user for direction (fix txn.py signing then flip, vs hold the flip).

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: USER DIRECTION: fix txn.py signing, THEN assess the store comprehensively for ALL operations still firing unsigned in-scope events (not just txn.py). Plan: (1) codebase sweep for every ticket-event write path that bypasses _apply_authorship; (2) fix them (txn transitions/claims/closes + any others) via held-out TDD; (3) confirm no ongoing unsigned in-scope writer; (4) then decide anchor + flip. Bug 0ba4 tracks the txn.py fix.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: STORE ASSESSMENT (per user direction): RECENT (signing-live) unsigned in-scope event types: STATUS(9), EDIT(6) [txn.py transitions/claims], FILE_IMPACT(4) [set-file-impact], TICKET_DIGEST(6), DONE_ENRICH(6)/ENQUEUE_ENRICH [enrich drain], SIGNATURE(2)/COMPLETION_VERDICT(1) [attestations], REVIEW_RESULT(4) [code_review = already exempt ticket type]. So MULTIPLE write paths bypass the signing seam, not just txn.py. Design question: route AUTHORED writes (STATUS/EDIT/FILE_IMPACT/...) through ONE shared finalize+sign seam (per user: no copy-paste); decide policy for SYSTEM/DERIVED events (TICKET_DIGEST/enrich/SIGNATURE/COMPLETION_VERDICT) = sign-if-keyed OR gate-exempt by event type (they are derived/attestation, not authored work). Architecture-map subagent running to produce the shared-seam design + full call-site inventory.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: FIX IMPLEMENTED (bug 0ba4): added shared finalize_event(event,ticket_id,event_type,data,tracker,repo_root) to _seam.py (attribution + _apply_authorship, no commit) — the ONE signing choke point. Routed append_event + txn.transition_core + txn.claim_core (transition/claim/close) + delete.py (_write_event/_write_unlink: STATUS(deleted)/ARCHIVED/UNLINK) through it; each keeps its own atomic commit/lock. Exemption + require_authenticated refusal live inside _apply_authorship so all callers inherit them. SNAPSHOT (compaction) intentionally left attribution-only: the merge-gate re-verifies the snapshot's authorship_ledger (preserved signed source events), not the SNAPSHOT event. Held-out oracle (test_identity_txn_signing_heldout.py, 5 tests): transition/claim/close STATUS+EDIT signed, verify under merge-gate, unsignable transition refused. ruff+mypy clean, 5/5 pass. Running full suite for regressions. Then teeth check + land via Gerrit + re-assess store for any remaining unsigned in-scope writers.
